{{one source |date=May 2024}}
In mathematics, '''Boas–Buck polynomials''' are sequences of polynomials <math>\Phi_n^{(r)}(z)</math> defined from [[analytic function]]s <math>B</math> and <math>C</math> by [[generating function]]s of the form

:<math>\displaystyle C(zt^r B(t))=\sum_{n\ge0}\Phi_n^{(r)}(z)t^n</math>.

The case <math>r=1</math>, sometimes called [[generalized Appell polynomials]], was studied by Boas and Buck (1958).<ref>{{Cite book |last=Boas |first=Ralph Philip |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eihMuwkh4DsC |title=Polynomial Expansions of Analytic Functions |last2=Buck |first2=Robert Creighton |date=1964 |publisher=Academic Press |isbn=978-0-387-03123-1 |language=en}}</ref>
